title: `actl dag` lets the main session change a ready ticket's dependencies and group (GitHub issues #9, #12; D-096)
objective: The main session changes a ready ticket's depends_on or group with one `actl dag` command, which refuses with one line and writes nothing for every change D-096 forbids.
outline: devloop/core/dagedit.py: given the pool data (tx.data), the ticket and the change (add, drop or to) plus by and why, it builds the changed dag.json entry and group fields in memory, checks them (core/dag.problems and core.chain.cycle on a Snapshot of the changed data, plus the refusals above), returns the refusal line or writes the change through tx (core.pool.new_group and event; member lists as core.pool.leave_group keeps them). devloop/dag_edit.py: argparse subcommands dep and move, Config() and pool_for() as tickets.py main does, a refusal printed on stderr as 'dag: <line>' with exit 2. bin/actl: 'dag' in the known-command case, `dag) exec python3 "$AC_HOME/devloop/dag_edit.py" "$@" ;;` and the TABLE line. Uses chain.order and chain.cycle from the chain-order ticket (#13) this one depends on.
test_plan: Verifier: acceptance 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 in a new file tests_devloop/test_dag_edit.py, class `DagEditAcceptance(LoopCase)`: groups written raw through self.pool.update with tx.put_group, tickets with self.add(..., group=...); the script through self.run_py('dag_edit.py', ...) and bin/actl through subprocess as test_controller.T51Acceptance.test_4_rerun_is_one_write_and_actl_runs_it_with_by_user does; pool HEAD via git rev-parse in self.pool_path. Expected values from this ticket. Implementer: unit tests of core/dagedit.py and acceptance 8 and 9 in a new class between MemberLeavesUnit and ChainGateUnits in tests_devloop/test_groups.py (not in test_dag_edit.py, which is the verifier's). Run only test_dag_edit, test_groups, test_chain, test_controller, test_pages, test_project_config, test_adapter_unittest and the base set.
notes: Group new-g2, after the chain-order ticket (#13) it depends on for chain.order and chain.cycle; the revise-with-DAG ticket depends on this one for core/dagedit.py. Only ready tickets change (D-096 item 3: running, merged and landed tickets are frozen, a stuck one is readied first). The '#M is cancelled' refusal is the opener's addition: a dependency on a cancelled ticket can never land, so N would wait forever. CLI only, not on the board (D-096 item 2). Never write the reporting project's name in code, tests or comments (tests/test_no_project_names.py forbids it in every non-markdown file): say 'the reporting project'.
acceptance: New command `actl dag`, mapped by bin/actl to a new script devloop/dag_edit.py and listed in bin/actl's TABLE as one line starting '  dag dep|move' (not on the board): `actl dag dep N --add M --reason R [--by B]`, `actl dag dep N --drop M --reason R [--by B]` (exactly one of --add/--drop) and `actl dag move N --to G --reason R [--by B]`, where G is an existing group id or the word new. --by defaults to 'main-session'.

A change is one pool write through pool.update; its checks run inside that write on the data it reads, before anything is written, in a new module devloop/core/dagedit.py (a later ticket reuses it for `actl new --revise`). On success the command exits 0 and its last stdout line is 'chain: ' followed by core.chain.order of the pool after the change, joined with ', '.

dep --add appends M to N's depends_on in dag.json; --drop removes it. Events, each with by and why (= the reason): on ticket N 'dag: depends on #M' / 'dag: no longer depends on #M'; on N's group and on M's group (each that exists and is not landed or cancelled; once when they are the same group) 'dag: #N depends on #M' / 'dag: #N no longer depends on #M'.

move sets N's 'group' to G (for new: a group made by core.pool.new_group with members [N], placed where the DAG puts it), clears N's 'target', removes N from its old group's members and appends it to G's. Events, each with by and why: ticket N 'dag: moved from <old group id, or no group> to <G's id>'; the old group 'dag: member #N moved to <G's id>'; G 'dag: member #N moved in from <old group id, or no group>' (for new this is the new group's first event). An old group left with no members becomes cancelled in the same write, with the event 'cancelled: its last member #N moved to <G's id>'.

Refused - exit 2, exactly one non-empty stderr line, nothing written (the pool's HEAD unchanged and its working copy clean) - checked in this order, the line containing: a missing or blank --reason: '--reason'; N unknown: '#N does not exist'; N not ready: '#N is <state>' (for merged and landed instead core.pool.frozen_reason's sentence, D-089, which contains '#N' and '(<state>)'); M unknown: '#M does not exist'; M == N: 'cannot depend on itself'; --add of a dependency N already has: 'already depends on #M'; --add of a cancelled M: '#M is cancelled'; --drop of one N does not have: 'does not depend on #M'; --drop M when N's objective, any acceptance item, test_plan, outline or notes contains '#M' not followed by a digit: 'mentions #M' and '`actl new --revise N`'; move to a group that does not exist: 'group G does not exist'; to a group that is not open (pr, fixing, verified, stuck, landed, cancelled): 'group G is <state>'; to N's own group: 'already in G'; a change that makes the ticket DAG a cycle: core/dag.problems' sentence starting 'cycle: '; one that makes the group order a cycle: 'the group order would be a cycle: ' followed by core.chain.cycle's path joined with ' -> '.

Cases, each on a fresh pool with groups written raw (created '2026-11-23T00:00:00Z'): (a) #1 ready in open g1, #2 ready in open g2: `dag_edit.py dep 1 --add 2 --reason r` exits 0, dag.json #1 depends_on ['2'], the last stdout line is 'chain: g2, g1', #1's last event has event 'dag: depends on #2', by 'main-session', why 'r', and g1 and g2 each have the event 'dag: #1 depends on #2'. (b) Then `dep 1 --drop 2 --reason r --by alice`: exit 0, depends_on [], 'chain: g1, g2', by 'alice'. (c) #1 the only member of g1, #2 in g2: `move 1 --to g2 --reason r`: g2 members ['2', '1'], #1's group 'g2', g1 cancelled with last event 'cancelled: its last member #1 moved to g2'. (d) #1 and #3 in g1, #2 in g2: `move 1 --to new --reason r`: a new group g3 with members ['1'] and first event 'dag: member #1 moved in from g1'; g1 members ['3']. (e) Each refusal of the previous item on its own fixture: exit 2, one stderr line with the named words, pool HEAD unchanged; the group-cycle fixture is #1 and #4 in g1, #2 and #3 in g2, #3 depending on #1, `dep 4 --add 2` -> 'the group order would be a cycle: g1 -> g2 -> g1'.
`actl dag dep 1 --add 2 --reason r` run through bin/actl from the project behaves as the script does, and `actl --help` lists the dag line.

## Issue #8: a regression's deadline starts when it has the machine
Observed in T (2026-11-23): g57's full regression waited for the machine behind g56, then had about 10 minutes left; the unit layers ran 554 s, test_browsers was stopped at the deadline after 40 s and the run was `unmeasured`.
Today devloop/regression.py `verify()` passes `began + regression_timeout_seconds` to `take`/`take_machine` and gives `_verify` the time left, so the wait is charged to the run (the module docstring says so).
Wanted: `regression_timeout_seconds` limits the run from the moment the slot or the whole machine is taken (preflight, quick, full and the flaky rerun share it). The wait for the machine gets its own limit: reuse an existing setting if one fits, otherwise add `devloop.regression_wait_seconds` with a default long enough for a full regression of another group to finish (say so in devloop/README.md); a wait that runs out is `unmeasured` with a summary saying it never got the machine, as today. Update the docstring.

## Issue #10: pages close when their subject is handled from any path
Observed in T (2026-11-23): the board showed 35 open pages, every one already answered or superseded: a group's "unmeasured" page after `actl tickets rerun gN`, tickets' "stuck" pages after `actl tickets ready N`, a fixer question after the group was readied, every `created` page.
Wanted:
- An action on a subject (a ticket or a group), through any path (CLI, board, `actl new --revise ... --decision`, `tickets ready`, `tickets rerun`, `tickets release`, `cancel`), acks every open decision/env page of that subject that the action answers, recording `acked_by` as the path (e.g. "tickets ready").
- When a subject moves on by itself (a stuck ticket is running again, an unmeasured group runs a regression again, a group or ticket lands or is cancelled), its older decision/env pages are acked with `acked_by: "superseded"`.
- `created` pages are information: the board's 要你判 tab and the waiting count do not count them (they stay listed in `tickets inbox`).
- Opener: grep every place that writes or reads `acked`, and every test that asserts pages stay open; list the tests that change.

## Issue #11: a controller restart does not kill in-flight regressions
Observed in T (2026-11-23 13:52Z): stopping `actl run --forever` and starting it again left g58 and g59 with "regression unmeasured - None" pages and no regression.py running; the g57 auto_fixer survived and was adopted. Jobs are started by osx.spawn with start_new_session=True, so the cause is not known.
Wanted: first reproduce it with the loop harness (start a controller, let it start a regression with a slow fake `full`, stop the controller with SIGTERM and with SIGINT, start a new one) and find the cause; write it in the ticket. Then fix it so a running regression survives the restart and is adopted like an auto_fixer: the new controller waits for it and reads its result. If the cause turns out to be outside A (for example how the user stopped the process on macOS), say so and make the controller report it instead of writing "unmeasured - None" (the page names what happened to the job).
